correctness.rationale: Staggering interchanges the band edges and removes signs from the finite-site resolvent by an orthogonal conjugation. The weighted Birman–Schwinger matrix decreases strictly in positive offset μ because the derivative quadratic form is the negative squared norm of the resolvent applied to a nonzero sum of distinct site vectors. The top-edge singularity is a positive rank-one logarithmic divergence plus the finite weighted Green difference −R/2, by dominated convergence for the difference. For any comparison level t off the limiting compression spectrum, a Schur complement of B_μ−tI in the divergent direction has exactly the limiting compression's inertia for sufficiently small μ, plus one positive direction; this identifies all finite limits with multiplicities. The positive congruence y_i=√κ_i x_i sends its complement to sum y_i=0 and transforms B−I's limiting finite form into Q. Strict decrease to zero gives exactly one crossing per limit above one and no crossing for equality. The two-point form on (1,−1) evaluates to R−1/κ_1−1/κ_2; the adjacent and diagonal resistances are 1/2 and 2/π, the latter also obtained by the torus change (x,y)=(u+v,u−v) and averaging sin²u/(1−cos u cos v). The compressed corner eigenvalues on the two displayed directions are 1/π and (π−1)/(3π). This verifies the thresholds and handles p=1 and all equalities without claiming a threshold-state classification. The above-band free resolvent decays exponentially and its convolution against finitely supported sources gives exponential localization. Independent finite-grid FFT-resolvent tests (python3 /workspace/review_evidence/reproduce.py 2) gave above-one counts [1,1,2,2,2,3,3] for seven mixed and equal noncritical pin sets; they are only corroboration.

evidence: Hayashi et al. use L=−P+V, where P is nearest-neighbour averaging, with arbitrary real nonzero strengths α_i at distinct sites. They count strict eigenvalues below −1 with multiplicity by p(QMQ)+1−m_+, with Q projecting off the constant site vector and M=diag(α_i)^(-1)+(g_ij).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Use α_i=−κ_i/4 and L=−P−diag_sites(κ)/4. With U the bipartite staggering, UHU=8I−4(I+L), so λ>8 maps bijectively with multiplicities to eigenvalues of L below −1. In d=2 the denominator of g_ij is (cos θ_1+cos θ_2)/2−1=−h(θ)/4 with h the unperturbed lattice symbol. Hence their g_ij=−2R(r_i−r_j). With m_+=0, QMQ on the zero-sum space is exactly four times the frozen form.

The two-pin and three-corner examples are direct finite evaluations of that prior theorem with known resistances, not independent surviving results.

value.rationale: The resistance interpretation is useful exposition for this natural physical model, but the frozen central assertion is a positive-pin specialization of an established exact (and stronger) theorem. The two- and three-pin claims are immediate one- and two-dimensional evaluations of the earlier compression using already known resistances. The package supplies no independently valuable unknown remainder that would justify a scientific repair.
